IVX HOLDINGS — OWNER AUTHENTICATION HARDENING
SUPABASE AUTH + IVX OWNER ACCESS
ROOT-CAUSE REPAIR + RESILIENCE + END-TO-END PRODUCTION CERTIFICATION

MISSION

Fix IVX owner sign-in permanently at the architecture level.

Do NOT solve this by:

- increasing the timeout
- adding more retry loops
- hiding errors
- bypassing Supabase
- restoring sessions without valid authentication
- creating another fallback auth system
- hard-coding owner access
- weakening security
- declaring success from backend-only tests

The goal is a deterministic owner authentication flow that is:

FAST
SECURE
OBSERVABLE
RECOVERABLE
IDEMPOTENT
CONSISTENT
PRODUCTION-VERIFIED

==================================================
CURRENT PRODUCTION FAILURE
==================================================

Observed live mobile error:

"Supabase Auth sign-in timed out after 30s."

Observed UX:

- owner enters email/password
- login waits
- app times out after approximately 30 seconds
- user remains locked out
- application offers controlled owner recovery
- owner authentication has been repeatedly unstable

This means previous login certification is invalid until the complete real owner login flow is verified from the production client.

==================================================
ARCHITECTURE PRINCIPLE
==================================================

Separate authentication from authorization.

Supabase must answer:

WHO IS THIS USER?

IVX backend must answer:

WHAT IS THIS USER ALLOWED TO DO?

Required architecture:

IVX CLIENT
    ↓
SUPABASE AUTH
    ↓
VALID SUPABASE SESSION / JWT
    ↓
IVX BACKEND
    ↓
OWNER PROFILE / MEMBERSHIP LOOKUP
    ↓
OWNER AUTHORIZATION
    ↓
APPLICATION SESSION READY
    ↓
NAVIGATE INTO IVX

Do not combine all of these stages into one opaque timeout.

==================================================
PART 1 — EVIDENCE GATE
==================================================

Before changing code:

1. Inspect the actual production authentication implementation.

2. Identify exact files responsible for:

- owner sign-in screen
- Supabase client initialization
- signInWithPassword call
- session persistence
- auth-state listeners
- secure token storage
- owner lookup
- backend owner verification
- owner recovery
- timeout wrapper
- navigation after login
- logout
- refresh token handling
- app startup session restore

3. Report exact file paths.

4. Determine whether there are multiple Supabase client instances.

5. Determine whether login invokes:

supabase.auth.signInWithPassword()

directly or through wrappers.

6. Identify every timeout and Promise.race involved in login.

7. Identify every useEffect/useFocusEffect/auth listener that may run during sign-in.

8. Identify every backend request triggered immediately after auth.

9. Identify all local/session storage reads and writes.

10. Identify all owner recovery code paths.

Do not change architecture until the real path is mapped.

==================================================
PART 2 — TRACE ONE LOGIN END TO END
==================================================

Create a login traceId.

Every login attempt must be traceable through:

LOGIN_TAP
CREDENTIAL_VALIDATION
SUPABASE_REQUEST_STARTED
SUPABASE_RESPONSE_RECEIVED
SESSION_CREATED
SESSION_PERSIST_STARTED
SESSION_PERSIST_COMPLETE
OWNER_LOOKUP_STARTED
OWNER_LOOKUP_COMPLETE
AUTHORIZATION_STARTED
AUTHORIZATION_COMPLETE
APP_SESSION_READY
NAVIGATION_STARTED
NAVIGATION_COMPLETE

Record:

traceId
timestamp
elapsedMs
checkpoint
success/failure
HTTP status when applicable
Supabase error code
IVX backend error
network error
timeout source

Never log:

password
access token
refresh token
secret keys

==================================================
PART 3 — IDENTIFY THE REAL 30 SECOND DELAY
==================================================

Do NOT assume Supabase consumes 30 seconds.

Measure independently:

T1
Login tap -> Supabase request started

T2
Supabase request start -> Supabase response

T3
Supabase response -> session persisted

T4
session persisted -> owner lookup start

T5
owner lookup start -> owner lookup result

T6
owner lookup -> authorization result

T7
authorization -> navigation complete

The final report must show exactly which segment is slow.

If:

signInWithPassword itself hangs:
diagnose Supabase/network/client issue.

If Supabase returns quickly:
the error text "Supabase Auth timed out" is misleading and must be corrected.

==================================================
PART 4 — REMOVE OPAQUE GLOBAL 30 SECOND TIMEOUT
==================================================

Audit any code resembling:

Promise.race([
    signIn(),
    timeout(30000)
])

A single wrapper around the complete authentication pipeline is forbidden.

Each stage must have independent timeout/error semantics.

Example conceptual boundaries:

Supabase network timeout
Owner API timeout
Storage timeout
Navigation timeout

If Supabase returns successfully, never report:

"Supabase Auth timed out"

because a later IVX operation failed.

Error messages must identify the actual failed layer.

==================================================
PART 5 — SUPABASE CLIENT SINGLETON
==================================================

Verify the app has exactly one intended Supabase client lifecycle.

Prevent:

- client recreation on rerender
- multiple auth listeners
- duplicate refresh loops
- competing storage adapters
- client instances with different URLs/keys
- login request from one client and session listener on another

Create/use a stable singleton Supabase client.

Verify client configuration once at startup.

==================================================
PART 6 — AUTH STATE LISTENER AUDIT
==================================================

Audit:

supabase.auth.onAuthStateChange()

Ensure:

- one intended subscription
- unsubscribe on cleanup when appropriate
- callback does not recursively call sign-in
- callback does not perform blocking work
- callback does not wait on slow network requests
- callback does not deadlock session persistence
- callback does not repeatedly navigate
- callback does not trigger duplicate owner lookups

Auth-state callbacks should be lightweight.

Heavy application initialization must occur outside the auth callback.

==================================================
PART 7 — SESSION PERSISTENCE
==================================================

Audit secure session persistence.

Determine what storage is used:

AsyncStorage
SecureStore
custom adapter
other

Verify:

- write completes
- read completes
- corrupted session is handled
- expired session is refreshed
- invalid refresh token produces controlled logout
- storage does not hang indefinitely

A storage failure must not masquerade as a Supabase login timeout.

==================================================
PART 8 — OWNER LOOKUP
==================================================

After a valid Supabase session exists:

perform a dedicated IVX owner authorization lookup.

Input:

authenticated Supabase user identity/JWT

Output:

authorized owner profile
or explicit denial

Possible results:

OWNER_AUTHORIZED
USER_AUTHENTICATED_NOT_OWNER
OWNER_RECORD_MISSING
BACKEND_UNAVAILABLE
TOKEN_INVALID
TOKEN_EXPIRED
PERMISSION_DENIED

Do not infer owner status merely from email on the client.

==================================================
PART 9 — BACKEND AUTHORIZATION
==================================================

The IVX backend must validate Supabase identity securely.

Verify:

- JWT signature validation
- expiration
- audience/issuer where applicable
- actual user ID
- owner record relationship
- role/permission mapping

Owner access must be determined server-side.

Never rely only on:

email string
client flag
local storage
"remember me"
previous UI state

==================================================
PART 10 — REMOVE DANGEROUS OWNER RECOVERY
==================================================

Audit the current message:

"Controlled owner recovery can still restore access on a previously verified owner device."

Determine exactly what this means.

Recovery must NOT bypass valid authentication.

A previously verified device must never become a permanent authentication substitute.

Allowed recovery mechanisms may include:

- valid persisted Supabase refresh session
- verified password reset
- secure reauthentication
- other established authenticated recovery

Forbidden:

- client-only owner flag
- previous device trust without valid session
- hidden bypass credential
- fallback hardcoded owner account
- unsigned locally generated session
- authorization based only on historical login success

If current recovery violates these rules, remove or redesign it.

==================================================
PART 11 — "REMEMBER ME"
==================================================

Define exactly what Remember Me means.

It may control persistence preference.

It must NOT:

- store plaintext password
- bypass authentication
- create an owner session independently
- turn an expired session into a valid session

If Supabase session persistence is already secure and automatic, simplify the feature.

==================================================
PART 12 — PASSWORD SECURITY
==================================================

Never log or persist plaintext password.

Never place password into:

logs
analytics
error traces
backend diagnostics
watchdog data
crash reports

Clear password field from memory/UI state when appropriate after successful login.

==================================================
PART 13 — NETWORK LAYER
==================================================

Audit connectivity from the production mobile app to Supabase.

Verify:

DNS
TLS
Supabase project host
IPv4/IPv6 behavior if relevant
mobile cellular network
Wi-Fi
Android networking
Expo/native networking
proxy configuration
VPN-related handling where applicable

Test real mobile network conditions.

Do not conclude "Supabase problem" without network evidence.

==================================================
PART 14 — RETRIES
==================================================

Do not blindly retry authentication.

Incorrect credentials:
NO automatic retry.

401/invalid credentials:
return immediately.

Network connection failure:
allow controlled retry.

5xx/temporary upstream issue:
limited retry only if appropriate.

Duplicate sign-in attempts must be prevented.

==================================================
PART 15 — IDEMPOTENCY / DOUBLE TAP
==================================================

One Sign In tap must initiate one logical login operation.

Disable or guard duplicate submission while the login attempt is active.

Prevent:

double tap
screen rerender
navigation refocus
auth listener
retry code

from creating duplicate concurrent signInWithPassword calls.

==================================================
PART 16 — LOGIN STATE MACHINE
==================================================

Create one canonical state machine.

Suggested states:

IDLE
VALIDATING
AUTHENTICATING
SESSION_READY
AUTHORIZING_OWNER
READY
FAILED
CANCELLED

The screen must derive from this state.

Do not maintain competing booleans like:

isLoading
isAuthLoading
isSupabaseLoading
isOwnerLoading
isRecovering
isNavigating

unless they are derived from the canonical state.

==================================================
PART 17 — FAIL FAST WITH ACCURATE ERRORS
==================================================

Errors must identify the failed stage.

Examples:

AUTH_INVALID_CREDENTIALS

"Email or password is incorrect."

NETWORK_UNAVAILABLE

"Cannot reach authentication service."

SUPABASE_TIMEOUT

"Authentication service did not respond."

OWNER_LOOKUP_TIMEOUT

"Signed in, but IVX could not verify owner access."

OWNER_NOT_AUTHORIZED

"Your account is authenticated but does not have owner access."

SESSION_PERSIST_FAILED

"Authentication succeeded but the local session could not be stored."

Do not call every failure:

Supabase Auth timeout.

==================================================
PART 18 — UI BEHAVIOR
==================================================

Expected user experience:

Tap Sign In

Immediately:

button becomes controlled loading state

Then either:

SUCCESS
navigate to IVX

or

ERROR
show one concise error

Do not show:

multiple overlapping dialogs
infinite spinner
30-second dead UI
duplicate alerts
conflicting recovery controls

Login screen must become usable immediately after failure.

==================================================
PART 19 — LOGIN PERFORMANCE
==================================================

Measure real timings.

Do not invent latency targets.

Record at minimum:

median
p95 if enough samples
worst observed

for:

Supabase authentication
owner lookup
complete sign-in

Run tests over:

Wi-Fi
cellular network
repeat login
cold app launch
warm app launch

==================================================
PART 20 — SESSION RESTORE
==================================================

Test app startup with:

valid session
expired access token + valid refresh token
expired refresh token
corrupted storage
no session
owner revoked
backend unavailable

Expected:

Valid session:
restore without requiring password.

Expired access token:
refresh appropriately.

Invalid refresh:
return to login.

Owner revoked:
deny application access even if Supabase session exists.

==================================================
PART 21 — LOGOUT
==================================================

Verify logout end to end.

Logout must:

- invalidate/clear active local session appropriately
- clear owner application state
- clear sensitive cached identity state
- stop authenticated subscriptions
- return to login

Test login -> logout -> login repeatedly.

==================================================
PART 22 — TOKEN REFRESH
==================================================

Audit token refresh lifecycle.

Verify:

- refresh happens once when required
- refresh does not produce duplicate auth events
- expired token does not hang backend requests
- refreshed token reaches IVX API correctly
- logout occurs on unrecoverable refresh failure

==================================================
PART 23 — API AUTH HEADER
==================================================

Verify every authenticated IVX backend request receives the active Supabase access token correctly.

Do not use stale tokens.

Audit:

Authorization: Bearer <token>

Verify token refresh updates the API layer.

==================================================
PART 24 — OWNER ACCESS CACHE
==================================================

If owner profile/permissions are cached:

define expiration/invalidation.

Do not permanently trust old owner authorization.

Revalidate at appropriate points.

==================================================
PART 25 — DATABASE / RLS
==================================================

Audit Supabase Row Level Security where owner data is accessed directly.

Verify:

RLS policies
authenticated role
owner identity relationship
service-role usage only on trusted backend

Do not expose service-role credentials to the client.

==================================================
PART 26 — SUPABASE CONFIGURATION
==================================================

Verify actual runtime configuration:

Supabase URL
public anon/publishable key
project environment
production vs development project
redirect configuration if applicable

Do not print secret values.

Report only:

PRESENT / MISSING / INVALID / MISMATCHED

==================================================
PART 27 — CREDENTIAL RULE
==================================================

Use credentials already present in the established IVX runtime/environment.

Do not ask the user for credentials by default.

First test whether existing runtime bindings work.

Only report credential intervention if actual evidence shows:

missing
expired
revoked
invalid
401
403
permission denied

Return exact error.

==================================================
PART 28 — MOBILE-SPECIFIC QA
==================================================

Test the actual IVX production mobile experience.

Required:

Android production build
cellular connection
Wi-Fi connection

Test:

cold launch login
warm launch login
wrong password
correct password
rapid Sign In tapping
background during sign-in
foreground during sign-in
network drop during sign-in
network return
logout/login
session restore

==================================================
PART 29 — FAILURE INJECTION
==================================================

Simulate/test where supported:

Supabase unavailable
IVX API unavailable
slow IVX API
bad password
expired JWT
owner lookup denial
storage failure
offline device

Ensure each failure produces the correct UI and cleanup.

==================================================
PART 30 — AUTOMATED TESTS
==================================================

Add tests for:

1. valid credentials success
2. invalid credentials immediate failure
3. Supabase timeout
4. owner lookup timeout
5. authenticated non-owner
6. session persistence failure
7. duplicate tap protection
8. auth-state listener single subscription
9. session restore
10. refresh success
11. refresh failure
12. logout
13. owner revocation
14. exact error mapping
15. no plaintext password logging
16. recovery cannot bypass authentication
17. backend receives current token
18. duplicate owner lookup prevention

Use existing project test infrastructure.

==================================================
PART 31 — REAL END-TO-END TEST
==================================================

A valid owner-login test must execute:

REAL PRODUCTION CLIENT
↓
REAL SIGN IN BUTTON
↓
REAL SUPABASE AUTH
↓
REAL SESSION
↓
REAL IVX BACKEND OWNER CHECK
↓
REAL AUTHORIZATION
↓
REAL APP NAVIGATION
↓
REAL AUTHENTICATED IVX SCREEN

Anything less is not end-to-end.

==================================================
PART 32 — PRODUCTION TEST SEQUENCE
==================================================

Test this exact sequence:

A.
Open production IVX app from fully closed state.

B.
Enter valid owner credentials.

C.
Tap Sign In once.

D.
Trace every checkpoint.

E.
Confirm Supabase session.

F.
Confirm owner authorization.

G.
Confirm authenticated IVX home screen.

H.
Close app.

I.
Reopen app.

J.
Confirm valid session restoration.

K.
Logout.

L.
Login again.

M.
Repeat on cellular.

N.
Repeat on Wi-Fi.

==================================================
PART 33 — NO FAKE CERTIFICATION
==================================================

A passing:

curl request
unit test
Supabase admin query
backend health check

does NOT by itself prove login works.

Do not declare complete unless real production client login passes.

==================================================
PART 34 — CI / BUILD
==================================================

Run actual available project commands for:

TypeScript
lint
unit tests
integration tests
Expo checks
Android build
backend tests

For every command report:

COMMAND
EXIT CODE
PASS/FAIL

No simulated results.

==================================================
PART 35 — DEPLOYMENT
==================================================

After changes:

commit
push
PR if required
CI
merge
Render/backend deploy if changed
Expo/mobile deployment/update if changed

Then verify actual production.

==================================================
PART 36 — SHA PARITY
==================================================

Verify:

GitHub HEAD
merged SHA
backend production SHA
health/version SHA if available

For mobile update/build, report actual production build/update identifier separately.

Do not call unrelated IDs SHAs.

==================================================
PART 37 — SECURITY REVIEW
==================================================

Before completion verify:

password never logged
JWT never logged
refresh token never logged
service role not exposed
owner status server-controlled
recovery cannot bypass auth
session storage appropriate
logout clears state
auth errors do not leak sensitive internals

==================================================
PART 38 — PREVIOUS LOGIN FIX AUDIT
==================================================

Review previous login fixes and certificates.

Determine:

- what was tested
- what was not tested
- why 30-second timeout remained
- whether tests only called backend endpoints
- whether they bypassed the real Supabase mobile path
- whether timeout was merely increased
- whether owner recovery hid the underlying problem

Report this explicitly.

==================================================
PART 39 — FINAL PASS/FAIL MATRIX
==================================================

Return exactly:

01 Supabase client singleton            PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED/UNVERIFIED

==================================================
PART 40 — REQUIRED FINAL REPORT
==================================================

Return:

A. ROOT CAUSE

Exact reason login reached 30-second timeout.

B. TIMING BREAKDOWN

C. AUTH ARCHITECTURE BEFORE

==================================================
PERMANENT ACCEPTANCE STANDARD
==================================================

Do not declare this fixed merely because one login succeeds.

The permanent acceptance standard is:

VALID OWNER LOGIN: PASS
INVALID PASSWORD HANDLING: PASS
SUPABASE AUTH: PASS
SESSION PERSISTENCE: PASS
TOKEN REFRESH: PASS
OWNER AUTHORIZATION: PASS
DUPLICATE PROTECTION: PASS
